title: The Machine Stops
pitch: Written in 1909, a short story about people living alone underground, served by a global Machine that meets every need, until it starts to fail.

chapters.g: Vashti lives in a cell, talks to thousands through screens, and reluctantly travels to see her son Kuno, who wants to visit the surface.
Kuno tells how he found a way to the surface and was dragged back by the Machine's repair system.
People come to worship the Machine. Then small faults grow, no one knows how to fix them, and the Machine stops.

ideas: Total dependence on a machine is fragile.
A system can become an object of worship.
Knowledge of how things work can be lost.

args.a: Forster predicted video calls, online lectures and life lived through screens.
args.c: It is a story, not a forecast, and it reflects worries of its own time.

args.a: Dependence on a system nobody understands is a serious risk.
args.c: Modern systems have backups and engineers, though complexity still grows.

questions: What in your life would stop if the internet stopped?
Who understands the systems you depend on?
Is the Machine aligned with its users?

quiz.q: Where do people live in the story?
What does Kuno want to do?
o: Visit the surface of the Earth
